title: POV: Mia Spends $410 on Halloween… You Spend $42 and Nobody Can Tell the Difference
description:
How to save money on Halloween without missing any of the fun: Mia spends $410, you spend $42, and nobody at the party can tell the difference.

In this POV story you make a costume from your own closet plus a $12 hat, buy candy once from a list (about 120 pieces, the week of Halloween, checking the unit price), reuse last year's decorations from one labeled bin, buy a $6 grocery-store pumpkin, host a potluck and leave the credit card at home. Then the November 1 move: post-Halloween clearance (often 50% off) only for things on your list, and a $10-a-month Halloween sinking fund so next year is already paid for.

👍 Subscribe to Simple Money Life for one simple money move every day.

Sources: NRF 2026 Halloween survey (expected record $13.5 billion total, about $115 per person, $4.4 billion on costumes, $4.3 billion on decorations, 96% of celebrants buying candy). Mia's and Sam's budgets are an example; your own costs and store discounts will differ.
